small_guidance:
- Sweep BLOCK_W ∈ {4, 8, 16} and num_warps ∈ {2, 4, 8} via `triton.autotune`; current 8/4 may not be optimal — the inner triple loop over (ddp,dhp,dwp)×KD×KH×KW×IC is heavy, so larger BLOCK_W with num_warps=8 could increase occupancy.
- Hoist the weight loads out of the spatial output loops: weights depend only on (kd,kh,kw,ic,oc) and are reloaded 8× (2×2×2) per program. Pre-load the entire (IC, OC, KD*KH*KW) tile once into registers/SRAM, then reuse across the 8 (ddp,dhp,dwp) iterations.
- Fuse the 2×2×2 pool window so the input gather is shared: many (d_out,h_out,w_out) positions in the pool window map to overlapping input voxels via the transpose-conv stride relation — compute the input index ranges once and reduce redundant loads.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as input-centric scatter-add: iterate over input voxels and scatter `x[n,ic,id,ih,iw] * W[ic,:,kd,kh,kw]` into the (d_out,h_out,w_out) output grid, then fuse maxpool/softmax/sub/swish/max in a second pass. The current gather form recomputes validity masks for every (kd,kh,kw) across 8 pool sub-positions; scatter avoids the modulo/stride masking entirely.
- Alternatively, switch to an implicit-GEMM form: for each output tile of (OC × spatial_tile), accumulate `W[ic,oc,k] @ X_gathered[ic,k,spatial]` with BLOCK_M=OC=16, BLOCK_N=spatial tile, BLOCK_K=IC*KD*KH*KW=81 — small enough to keep in registers, and tl.dot will use tensor cores.
- Make OC the contiguous inner GEMM-M dim (OC=16 fits one warp); persist the per-(n,dp,hp) state and stream through wp tiles so the softmax/swish/max epilogue runs on registers without re-reading a materialized (N,OC,Dp,Hp,Wp) tensor.
